statement: A running model, not a calibrated one. Sizes of leaf, flower and capsule, the length of stem made in a summer and the season of flowering are from published descriptions; how many stems a plant makes, how long a flower lasts, how much seed sets in Britain, every date and every weight in the stem's mechanics are assumptions, and the weights in a shoot's choice of way are chosen to reproduce how a gardener trains it. None has been measured on a plant. An annual here cannot branch or thicken in its one year, so its branches are entered as stems from the base. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: One leaf form, one flower form, one fruit form. The flower stands singly on a stalk 3 to 9.5 cm long from the leaf axil (Weeds of Australia) and faces out from the support and a little up; the capsule ripens on the same stalk inside the same two bracts, beak outwards.

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: Not bud break: the first day on which a plant in the ground is taken to grow, mid May. It is set out once the frosts are over (RHS Plants: planted out "after all risk of frost has passed, 30cm (12in) apart"; Wisconsin Extension: when nights stay above 50 F). The day itself is a choice.

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: Taken to go on extending until the nights turn cold in mid October: a tropical African plant rated H2, "Tolerant of low temperatures but will not survive being frozen" (RHS hardiness ratings, H2). No dated source; in a real year it is the weather that decides.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: Not a flush: there is no old wood to leaf out. Every leaf stands on growth of the year and opens as that growth is made; the window only has to begin before the plant is set out.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: Not used. The plant is evergreen by habit (RHS), and the engine gives an evergreen leaf no autumn colour: its leaves are drawn green until the day the cold kills it. What the leaves of a British plant do in the last cold weeks is not recorded in any source read. The window is kept inside the plant's last fortnight because every model carries every parameter.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Not leaf fall: the plant is killed by the cold, taken as the first week of November, and its last day is the day it dies. RHS hardiness H2 (1 to 5 degC, "Tolerant of low temperatures but will not survive being frozen"). The date stands for the first hard frost, which in a real year comes when it comes.

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: Day-neutral, and able to flower six weeks from seed (PanAmerican Seed, Susie series: "Daylength: Day Neutral", "can pop into flower in as little as 6 weeks"), so nothing but size holds a plant back: buds are taken to form from late June on a plant set out in mid May, and on every node made after that.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: Flowers open one after another along the growing stems "from summer to early autumn" (RHS): taken as 1 July to 7 October. Seed houses give June or July to October; Wisconsin Extension "bloom from mid-summer to frost".

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: Not used: each flower lasts its own few days (phenology.flowerLastsDays). Kept inside the flowering season because every model carries every parameter.

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: How long a node is in flower. No source gives the life of one corolla. A photograph of a seed-grown plant (Wikimedia Commons: "Black Eyed Susan (Thunbergia alata) with orange flowers.jpg") shows two or three successive nodes of one shoot in flower together; at a node every three or four days that is about a week to a node, whether as one corolla or as the two axils flowering in turn, which the engine cannot tell apart since it gives a node one flower. Unmeasured, and the number of flowers open at once follows from it directly.

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: The most stem one shoot makes in a summer: "reaching up to 8 feet in a single season under ideal conditions" (Wisconsin Extension), which is 2.4 m; RHS "to 2.5 m tall". Most stems stop short of it, at the length drawn for each from architecture.leaderLengthM: the breeder gives the vine length of the Susie series as 1.8 to 2 m, and Wisconsin 3 to 5 ft as usual in the Midwest.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Never used for this plant as the engine stands: a branch breaks in the spring after its bud was laid down, and an annual has no second spring. Its branches are entered as further stems from the base instead (architecture.trunkStemStartYears).

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: Never used: long shoots of the year are thrown by stems of earlier years, and this plant has none.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: No slow first year: its first summer is its only one, and a pot-grown plant set out in warm soil grows away at once.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: Twenty-four twining stems in the year it is planted, standing for the seedling's own stem and every branch it makes. It branches from the leaf axils all summer; sources say only "many twining stems" (SANBI, as a search result gives it: the page could not be opened) and "one or many stems" (Botany Brisbane). The engine cannot branch a stem in the year it is made, so every branch is entered here as a stem from the ground, and all start on planting day, which real branches do not. The number is chosen, not counted, from what the plant is said to cover and what photographs show: a spread of 0.5 to 1 m and a height of 1.5 to 2.5 m (RHS), clothed as a column of overlapping leaf two or three deep (Wikimedia Commons: "Thunbergia alata, Hungary.jpg", "Climber at timber-framed house, Limburg.jpg"). Such a column 0.6 m wide and 1.8 m high, two to three leaves deep, holds about 900 to 1300 leaves of this size, which at a pair of leaves every 9 cm is 40 to 60 m of stem; 24 stems of 1.5 to 2.5 m make about 47 m.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: Set out as a small pot plant of eight to ten weeks (PanAmerican Seed: four to five weeks in the plug and four to five more to finish in a 10 cm pot). Its length then is not given; 0.2 m is a choice.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Never reached: no bud of this plant lives to break into a branch (see extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder).

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: How long a stem may get: the RHS ultimate height of 1.5 to 2.5 m, which agrees with the breeder's vine length of 1.8 to 2 m and the 3 to 8 ft of the American extension services. A height band is not a route length; here it bounds stem length.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Never used for this plant: see extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: Not used for this plant: an annual here makes no branch from a bud, since a bud breaks only in a later spring and this plant has none (see extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder). The value is kept because every model carries every parameter.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: Not used for this plant: no bud of an annual lives to a second spring to break into a branch; its branches are entered as stems from the base (architecture.trunkStemStartYears). Kept because every model carries every parameter.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: Buds do not wait a year: there is no second year.

architecture.budExtraDormancyYears.basis: Not used: buds of this plant never wait a year (architecture.budExtraDormancyChance is 0). Kept because every model carries every parameter.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: As many as the plant has. The stems are a millimetre or two thick and wind round one another as readily as round the support, so a plant given one string sends every stem up it as a single rope. Not a count from a source.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: As many as the plant has: a gardener can tie any number of stems a millimetre or two thick up a glulam member. Not a count from a source.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: How much a stem is put off a support by each stem already on it. A gardener training this plant on a trellis spreads its stems across it: the RHS gives it a spread of 0.5 to 1 m beside its 1.5 to 2.5 m of height, and photographs of plants on a frame show a column of leaf as wide as a lath bay or two (Wikimedia Commons: "Thunbergia alata, Hungary.jpg"), not a rope. At 1.5 the first stems take the stay cable, which they twine by themselves, and the rest go to the post and the trellis, where they are tied. A weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement; raised from the draft's 0.6, at which twelve of eighteen stems went up the one cable.

routing.downhillCostPerM.basis: What a stem is put off by each metre a way runs downhill. A twining shoot does not wind downhill, and a gardener does not lead one down: at 40 a stem follows a drop of at most 0.35 m before it gives up (routing.giveUpCost), and prefers a crowded upright to a lath that runs down to the ground, which at 10.7 one stem in two dozen took. How far a shoot of this plant will go down a support is not recorded. A weight, not a measurement.

routing.uphillBonusPerM.basis: A twining shoot climbs: its tip sweeps round until it meets something upright and winds up it. Set so that a rise of 0.4 m is worth as much as the largest chance element in the choice (routing.noise), which at the value copied from wisteria it was not. A weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement.

routing.straightOnBonus.basis: No leaning towards carrying straight on. A woody leader keeps its line; the tip of this plant circles as it grows (Darwin timed a circle at about three hours) and takes the first upright it meets. At 0 a stem led along a rail turns up the next free upright it comes to.

routing.riserBonus.basis: A pull towards rising members for a stem the engine marks as a riser. This plant's stems all climb by twining, and routing.uphillBonusPerM already gives every stem its wish to go up; the value is a weight in the engine's choice of route, chosen so that a riser still prefers an upright lath to a level rail. Not a measurement.

routing.tierBonus.basis: No stem of this plant is set on running level: every one climbs. The engine marks all stems after the first for a lowest tier, which is a way of training wisteria; at 0 that mark does nothing here.

routing.roleDropChance.basis: The chance that a stem marked for a level tier or a riser forgets its mark. With routing.tierBonus at 0 the mark does nothing for this plant, so the chance changes nothing that is drawn. Not a measurement.

routing.noise.basis: The chance element in a stem's choice of way at a joint. The tip of this plant circles as it grows and takes whatever it meets first (Darwin timed a circle at about three hours), so the choice between two rising ways is close to a toss; 0.9 is worth a rise of about 0.45 m at routing.uphillBonusPerM, enough to split stems between the post and the laths without sending any down. A weight, not a measurement.

routing.giveUpCost.basis: The cost at which a stem gives up rather than take the cheapest way on. Raised from the 4.2 copied from wisteria so that a support already carrying stems does not stop the next one: with routing.occupancyCost at 1.5 and two dozen stems from one foot, at 9 the last stem to leave the foot found every way too crowded and grew not at all. A gardener ties every stem in somewhere, and this plant's stems wind round one another as a matter of course. A weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: No measurement exists. Darwin grew a dozen plants on "sticks of various thicknesses" and on string and all twined them, without giving a thickness; growers give it canes, netting, wire and string. A slender herbaceous twiner, taken to hold anything up to a stout cane and nothing as thick as a 40 mm lath.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: How far the stem climbs in one turn round a thin support. No source gives the pitch of its coils; a real stem probably coils tighter than this, about a turn to an internode. The engine stores a stem as points 4 cm apart, so 0.16 m, four points to the turn, is the tightest coil it can draw as a coil at all.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: How far a coil climbs per circumference of the support round which it winds, beyond attachment.minPitchM. No source gives the coils of this plant; on the thin cables and strings it is given, the minimum pitch decides the coil and this ratio matters only round thicker supports. Not a measurement.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: Stem between one pair of leaves and the next. The only figure found is "four and a half to 13 centimeters" between leaf stalks, in an encyclopedia article that names no flora for it and could not be traced to one; it is used as the best there is and labelled as unverified.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: From the stem to the farthest point of the leaf as it hangs, which is what the engine calls the length of a leaf and what the drawing measures: the stalk and the blade hung from its top at about 50 degrees below the stalk's line (morphology.json leaf.bladeDropDeg, read from photographs), so the stalk plus 0.64 of the blade. Blades "about 3-8 x 3-7.5 cm" on stalks "about 2.5-3.5 cm long" (Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants): 2.5 + 0.64 x 3 = 4.4 cm, and 3.5 + 0.64 x 7.5 = 8.3 cm, the top of the blade range taken as 7.5 cm, the "up to 3 inches" of Wisconsin Extension and North Carolina State, since plants of one summer in Britain do not make the largest leaves. The draft's 5.5 to 11 cm was stalk and blade laid end to end, which drew every blade a quarter too large once the viewer hung it.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: Leaves opposite, in pairs (Weeds of Australia; Wisconsin Extension; Darwin: "the opposite leaves of Thunbergia alata").

organs.spurChance.basis: No spurs: no wood lasts long enough to bear them.

organs.spurLengthM.basis: Not used: no spurs are modelled for this plant.

organs.spurLeafCount.basis: No spurs are modelled for this plant.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: Width of the one flower across its five spread lobes: "3-4 cm wide" (Weeds of Australia); "1½ inch wide" (Wisconsin Extension). The flowers stand singly, so one flower is one record.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: No side shoots from old stems: there are no old stems.

organs.whipsPerYearMax.basis: No side shoots from old stems: there are no old stems.

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: Evergreen where it is warm enough (RHS); outdoors in the UK a leaf lasts from its unfolding until the cold kills the plant.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: Flowers in the summer it is planted: grown as an annual, and in flower six to ten weeks from seed (PanAmerican Seed).

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: Flowers stand singly in the leaf axils (Weeds of Australia: "borne singly in the upper leaf forks"), and a node has two axils. The engine can give a node one flower a year, so every node long enough made is given one: 11.5 a metre at the mean spacing of the leaf pairs. How many axils of a real plant flower is not recorded.

flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM.basis: The first few nodes of a stem bear leaves only; taken as its first 0.2 m. Not from a source.

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant (RHS: "No pruning required outdoors"); present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: Shoots from below a cut. Never used: the gardener does not cut this plant (RHS: no pruning needed outdoors), and no event in its routine cuts a stem. Kept because every model carries every parameter.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A stem 1.6 mm thick. Two unverified figures bracket it: "one to one and a quarter millimeter thick" in an encyclopedia article that names no flora, and "slender (ca. 2 mm)" in a guide text. As the engine stands this is the thickness of every stem for its whole life: stems are thickened at the year's end, and this plant is dead by then.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Never applied: thickening is worked out on 31 December for living plants, and the cold has killed this one in November. Were it applied, the foot of a 2 m stem would be about 3 mm thick, which is what the base of a plant looks to be by autumn; not measured.

thickening.branchShare.basis: How a stem's thickening is shared at a fork. Never applied: stems are thickened at the year's end and this plant is killed by the cold in November (thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2). Kept because every model carries every parameter.

fruit.setShare.basis: One flower in five is taken to set a capsule outdoors in Britain. Seed "is often produced late in the season" (Wisconsin Extension) and the plant seeds itself where it is warm; how much sets in a British summer is not recorded anywhere found.

fruit.lengthM.basis: The capsule from its foot to the end of its beak. Built from published sizes and one photograph: a base 5-10 mm across and a beak 9-15 mm long (Weeds of Australia), the base about 0.7 as high as it is wide (Wikimedia Commons: "Kapselfrucht.jpg"), so 3.5 to 7 mm of base and 9 to 15 mm of beak. The stalk and the two bracts are not counted.

fruit.swellDays.basis: Days from the fall of the corolla to a full-sized green capsule. No source; taken as two to three weeks.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: The capsule "ripens and dries (RC) to a tan color" inside its bracts (Wisconsin Extension), "often produced late in the season". Taken as August to late October; no dated British record found.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: A ripe capsule splits down its beak and throws its seeds; what is left of it is taken to go at some time between then and the plant's death. No source for how long the empty husk stays. Whatever is left goes with the plant when the cold kills it.

appendages.tendrilNodePattern.basis: No tendrils: "rather than by clinging or producing tendrils as some other vines do" (Wisconsin Extension); it holds on by twining its stems.

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: The leaf stalks do not coil: every description has the stems twining and none the stalks. Darwin, who grew a dozen plants, lists it among stem twiners.

appendages.leafStalkLengthM.basis: No coiled leaf stalks: see appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.

appendages.aerialRootPatchSpacingM.basis: No clinging rootlets. Stems that trail on the ground root at the nodes (Botany Brisbane), which is not a hold on a support.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Unarmed: a soft, hairy herb. No description mentions prickles.

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: None. Its branches are long twining stems like the one that bears them, and its flowers stand in the leaf axils of all of them; it has no short shoot that ends in a flower.

mechanics.greenShootModulusMPa.basis: How stiff the green stem is. Never measured on this plant. A soft herbaceous stem that never lignifies outdoors here; the value is the generic green shoot's, at the bottom of the searcher stiffnesses Hattermann and others measured across 29 climbers (213 to 15 479 MN/m2). Decides nothing drawn while every stem of this plant is a leader on a route: the engine lays only shoots in the air by their weight, and this plant makes none.

mechanics.woodModulusMPa.basis: How stiff the stem is once set. This plant makes no wood in its one British summer, so the set stem is taken as barely stiffer than the green one; no measurement found. Decides nothing drawn while the plant makes no shoot in the air.

mechanics.woodSetDays.basis: Days a length of stem stays green and soft: longer than this plant lives outdoors in Britain (set out mid May, killed in early November), so in effect it never sets. Not a measurement.

mechanics.stemFreshDensityKgM3.basis: Fresh density of the stem, taken as that of water, as for a soft herbaceous stem; not weighed.

mechanics.leafFreshMassPerAreaKgM2.basis: Fresh mass of leaf for each square metre of the disc the engine takes for a leaf. A thin, soft blade (Wisconsin Extension: "soft and hairy"); not weighed. The generic figure, a film of water a fifth of a millimetre thick.

mechanics.inflorescenceFreshMassKg.basis: One flower with its stalk and two bracts: a corolla about 3 to 4 cm across and 1.5 to 2.5 cm of tube (Weeds of Australia), taken as a gram and a half; not weighed.

mechanics.fruitFreshMassKg.basis: One capsule, a round base 5 to 10 mm across and a beak 9 to 15 mm long (Weeds of Australia), with its bracts: taken as under a gram; not weighed.

mechanics.searcherReachM.basis: How far a shoot holds itself out unsupported before its weight brings it over. No figure for this plant; Hattermann and others give stem twiners 0.10 to 2.25 m, and a thread of a stem a millimetre or two thick is near the bottom of that range. Not used while the plant makes no shoot in the air.

tropism.turnPerM.basis: How fast a free shoot turns to the vertical and the light. The generic value; no measurement of this plant. Not used while the plant makes no shoot in the air.

tropism.lightShare.basis: How far a free shoot leans to the light rather than straight up. The generic value; not used while the plant makes no shoot in the air.

mechanics.leanDeg.basis: The lean of a shoot that would set out plumb. The generic value; not used while the plant makes no shoot in the air.

mechanics.leafWeightOffsetShare.basis: How far off the stem a leaf's weight acts, as a share of its length. The generic value; not used while the plant makes no shoot in the air.

attachment.graspReachM.basis: How wide a gap a circling tip crosses to take hold. Darwin timed this plant's tip round a circle in about three hours but gave no width for its sweep; a shoot this slender sweeps less than the hop's 19 inches. A choice, not a measurement.

organs.leafTurnToOpenShare.basis: How far each leaf stalk is turned away from what the stem lies on, towards the open side and the light. Photographs of plants on a post and on wires show the leaves standing out from the support and lying over one another face outwards, nearly none turned in to it (Wikimedia Commons: "Thunbergia alata, Hungary.jpg", "Black Eyed Susan (Thunbergia alata) with orange flowers.jpg"). A share read from pictures, not a measurement.
